newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks snap losing streak to close up.
newsitem.headline: French stocks snap losing streak to close up.

text.p: French stocks snapped a week-long losing streak on Monday to finish higher, helped by firmer bond prices and bullish oil stocks.
Trading was extremely thin with volume totalling just 2.3 billion francs -- around half the average -- due to the closure of the U.S. markets for the Labor Day holiday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 6.37 points, or 0.32 percent, at 1,976.98, while the CAC-40 September futures contract rose eight points to 1,981.
Shares in oil companies Elf Aquitaine and Total rose on the United Nations' move to postpone Iraq's return to oil markets -- a decision that lifted oil prices.
Total closed up 1.99 percent at 379.90 francs, while Elf shares rose 2.22 percent to 376.90.
Iraqi military activity in the Kurdish north led the U.N. to delay a planned Iraqi oil-for-food exchange, stopping the first sales of Iraqi oil since the Gulf War six years ago.
Brokers said the oil shares were also bolstered by expectations of good first-half results, due later this week.
Euro Disney shares jumped 0.55 franc to 12 after Chairman Philippe Bourguignon said in a newspaper interview that the theme park operator was on track for a second annual profit.
Traders say the bourse will probably trade in a narrow range ahead of the U.S. August jobs report due out on Friday and the French 1997 budget due to be unveiled on September 10.
